## What to Build

`cmd/partio/status.go` checks whether Partio's hooks are installed using `os.Stat` alone — it verifies that the hook files exist but does not inspect their content. When another hook manager (Lefthook, Husky, Overcommit) installs or reinstalls hooks, the hook files at those paths exist but no longer contain Partio's marker. `partio status` continues to report `Hooks: installed`, so the user sees a healthy status while session capture is silently off.

`cmd/partio/doctor.go` already solves this correctly: it reads each hook file and checks for the string `"partio _hook"` (lines 54–58). The fix is to apply the same content check in `status.go`'s hook-verification block.

Replace the `os.Stat`-only check in `status.go` (lines 66–78) with a loop that reads each hook file and calls `strings.Contains(string(data), "partio _hook")` — the same check `doctor.go` uses — and marks `allInstalled = false` when a file is missing **or** does not contain the Partio marker.


**Notes (argos review, 2026-10-12; #704 closed as a duplicate).** Test the marker line `# Installed by partio` (`partioMarker`, `internal/git/hooks/hooks.go:8`, the test that `isPartioHook` uses at install), not the text `partio _hook`. #698 quotes the binary path of `--absolute-path` hooks (`"/path/partio" _hook`), and the text test then fails for each such hook. Export one helper from `internal/git/hooks` and use it in `status` and in `doctor` (`doctor.go:58` has the same text test). Related: #344. When `core.hooksPath` is set, git runs the hooks of that directory, so the Partio files in `.git/hooks` never run, and this check still says `installed`.
## Why This Matters

A developer who ran `partio enable`, then reinstalled their hook manager (e.g., `lefthook install`), then ran `partio status` would see `Hooks: installed`. Sessions captured by `pre-commit` / `post-commit` stop appearing, but the status surface says nothing is wrong. Running `partio doctor` would catch this, but `status` is the first command users reach for. Closing the gap between the two commands means a mismatched hook stack is visible immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `partio status` shows `Hooks: installed` only when every hook file exists **and** carries the Partio marker `# Installed by partio`
- [ ] When a hook file exists but lacks the marker, `partio status` shows `Hooks: missing (run 'partio enable' to reinstall)`
- [ ] When a hook file is entirely absent, behaviour is unchanged from today
- [ ] Test covers the case where the hook file exists with foreign content (not `"partio _hook"`) and asserts that `allInstalled` is `false`
- [ ] `status` and `doctor` use one shared check, and a hook installed with `--absolute-path` shows as installed in both

## Premise

<!-- partio:premise:v1 -->

- `cmd/partio/status.go` checks hook installation using `os.Stat` only, without reading hook file content [evidence: `cmd/partio/status.go`]
- `cmd/partio/doctor.go` checks hook file content for the string `"partio _hook"` to determine ownership [evidence: `cmd/partio/doctor.go`]

## Gathered Evidence

**Claim 1 — `status.go` uses `os.Stat` only**
Evidence: `cmd/partio/status.go`
Verdict: `holds`
Excerpt: lines 66–78 — `for _, h := range hooks { if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(hooksDir, h)); err != nil { allInstalled = false; break } }` — no file read, no content check.

**Claim 2 — `doctor.go` checks content for `"partio _hook"`**
Evidence: `cmd/partio/doctor.go`
Verdict: `holds`
Excerpt: lines 54–58 — `data, readErr := os.ReadFile(hookPath) ... else if strings.Contains(string(data), "partio _hook") { fmt.Printf("[OK]   %s hook installed\n", name) } else { fmt.Printf("[WARN] %s hook exists but not managed by partio\n", name) }`
